openings.claim: Self-contained starters may reduce topic-history barriers while retaining the familiar sequence. A1 additionally proposes neutral immediate pairing, equal timed turns, optional simpler/extended prompts and odd-attendance triads; partner changes remain voluntary.
openings.discriminator: Separate pairing delay, content familiarity and airtime: faster pairing or equal turns without improved reported usefulness is insufficient.
openings.probe: Z1 randomizes pairs between usual prompts and self-contained openings, allowing switching. A1 observes six sessions. Record entry delay, partner changes, speaking distribution, usefulness, optional anonymous familiarity and volunteer time.
openings.uncertainty: Entry causes remain unknown; proficiency mismatch is unproven. Added preparation/timing must fit existing resources.

openings.claim: Z2 proposes a consistently placed dated next-task box to resolve temporal confusion. A2 adds a reusable card with one standalone task, closing read-aloud, universal handout and current information on arrival, potentially reducing clarification work.
openings.discriminator: Separate correct, earlier and blank answers; fewer earlier answers without fewer blanks limits temporal explanation. Fewer messages without total workload below 90 minutes is insufficient.
openings.probe: Z2 alternates usual/dated sheets over six sessions with arrival/departure print access. A2 checks all attendees' identification, anonymous print-only access and printing/topic/message/access time.
openings.uncertainty: Details must be settled before printing and understandable; attendance confounds comparisons, and added printing may offset savings.

decision: Probe both; no effectiveness established. Preserve free inclusive participation, offline access, conversational purpose, 75 minutes and existing volunteers. Evaluate six-session 80% useful-speaking, 85% preparation and <90-minute coordination targets. Baseline slips cover 72/97 attendances; speaking was untimed and responses unlinked.
